rv.q: Fiasco's more moderate course still feels welcoming and genuine. It's here to spin a good yarn.
It’s Fiasco’s best work to date.
Now I’d like to think that if I ever see another Pericles , it’s a revival of this nifty Fiasco rigmarole.
Pericles courses along, always accessible, but it seldom leaps off the stage into something that enchants.
The ramshackle approach seems fitting for a plot-dense story that seems like a mashup of Shakespearean tropes...
